doc.title: Dave Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007

title: Bach and Beethoven analogy and closing thanks
summary: Dave argues jazz should keep old styles as classical music does, and the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: I mean it’s not really the song, it’s really in how it’s approached, what they’re doing with it. But yeah we need the brass band sound to continue to evolve, we need everything to continue to evolve. We just need to, as things evolve, we need to remain proud of what’s come before and not feel like we’re doing something bad by continuing to enjoy it and continuing to play it. I think young people need to be inspired to believe that they can be just as self-realized in an older style as in a newer one and that the older styles don’t lose their relevance just because they first popped up many years ago. We don’t do that in classical music. We don’t throw out Bach and Beethoven to listen to Schoenberg. Do we? I mean you go to Carnegie Hall you’ll hear Schoenberg one night and you’ll hear Bach and Beethoven the next night.
More Bach and Beethoven than Schoenberg.
Yeah right. So why do we have to do that in jazz and popular music?
It’s a darn good question and I appreciate your efforts.
Well I’m glad you came by today and thanks for your time.
Well I’m flattered. Thanks very much.
